post.summary:
Stop the running planner turn. Guard chain mirrors `/planner/input` but WITHOUT lazy recovery: a harness that needs recovering has no running turn to stop, so a registry miss is the same 409 `planner_harness_dormant`.
Idle is a graceful no-op (`stopped: false`). The phase read and the dispatch are not atomic; the user presses Stop again.
`IssuingTurn` also reports `stopped: false`: while `turn/start` is in flight the app-server may not know the turn yet, so the interrupt is dispatched best-effort but only `TurnRunning` guarantees a target.

200.description: Interrupt dispatched at the running turn (`stopped: true`); `stopped: false` when no turn was running (graceful no-op) or a turn was still being issued (best-effort dispatch only — press Stop again once the turn is running)

patch.summary:
PATCH semantics: absent keys keep their stored value, an explicit `null` deletes the
key. Stored keys the schema no longer declares are kept in the row but excluded from
validation. `required` is enforced at consumption, not here. Gate order is
`404 → 409 → 400`. Taking effect needs an explicit `POST /api/plugins/{id}/reload`.

parameters.name: reset
parameters.description:
Discard the stored `user_config` entirely and apply this patch to an empty object.
The recovery action for a corrupt (non-object) row; on a healthy row it means
"reset this plugin to its manifest defaults".

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
**Required if the body carries `first_message`; optional otherwise, and honoured when sent.** A create that sends no key at all is not idempotent — a retry mints a second track — which is the unchanged behaviour of every caller that sends none.

Without `first_message`, a key binds the minted track and nothing else: an identical repeat returns that same track with 201, a different create shape under the same key is 409 `conflict`, and no retry slot is consumed (so this shape cannot exhaust a key). Adding or removing `first_message` under a key already bound by the other shape is itself a 409 `conflict`, in both directions.

With `first_message`, one transaction persists the minted track/card ids and a versioned fingerprint of the original create. The fingerprint covers every mint input (`title`, `sort`, the original `cwd`, `template_id`, `recipe_id`, `template_input`, `attach_folder`, `theme`, `fork_report_from`, non-null `model` / `reasoning_effort`, and a `planner_provider` other than `codex`) plus the initial message digest, so it still constrains the key when no operation row exists. A different create shape is always 409 `conflict`, including after a terminal operation failure. A different `first_message` is also a conflict after success, `Stuck`, or a pre-operation failure; it may be edited only after a persisted terminal `Failed` attempt, where the fresh `#N` operation key represents a new delivery attempt against the same track.

An identical request after success returns the same track without re-delivery. A persisted terminal failure genuinely retries; a `Stuck` attempt keeps replaying its recorded 500; 64 failed attempts exhaust the key. Resume does not rerun mutable create-path validation, so repointing or deleting an attached workspace does not change request identity. Bindings created before request fingerprints existed fail closed with 409 because the server cannot prove request equality.

201.description: Track created. With `first_message`, the message is also queued for the planner agent inside the harness-start transaction; a retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same track without re-delivering it.

400.description: Malformed create (bad `cwd`, unknown `template_id`, invalid `template_input`, a `planner_provider` this server cannot run, `claude` with a `model` that is not one of its aliases (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`) or with any `reasoning_effort`, or `reasoning_effort` unsupported by the selected model's current catalog entry; no track is minted and no effort is silently adjusted), more than one of `template_id` / `recipe_id` / `fork_report_from` (each names a starting point; give at most one — naming none is the ordinary blank create), a malformed `Idempotency-Key` header (empty or non-ASCII) on any create, or — with `first_message` — a missing `Idempotency-Key` or an empty/over-long message. Decided before anything is minted; the multi-source refusal, like every other create-path check, is not re-run on an `Idempotency-Key` replay, which mints nothing.

409.description: Folder-claim conflict (structured `FolderConflict` body), `conflict` when an `Idempotency-Key` is bound to a different create or to a legacy binding whose request cannot be proven, or `idempotency_key_exhausted` when the key used all 64 retry slots, when the track it names has been deleted, or when its managed workspace can no longer be materialized. Recovery depends on `code`: fix a folder conflict and retry the same key; preserve the original request for a payload conflict (use a new key only for an explicit new create); use a new key after `idempotency_key_exhausted`.

500.description: Internal error. One case leaves the track behind: when the request carried a `first_message` and the planner harness start did not complete, the track, its cards and its workspace are already committed, and whether the message reached the agent is **unknown to the server** — depending on how far the start got, it may never have been handed over, or it may already have been delivered and answered. Nothing is rolled back and nothing compensates. What the server *can* promise, and this is what the `Idempotency-Key` buys: retrying the identical request under the **same** key creates no second track and delivers no second copy of the message. It does not promise the track is usable — a replay does not repair an attached workspace whose directory was deleted. Without `first_message` the same harness failure is logged and still returns 201, because no user text was riding on it — which also holds when such a create sends an `Idempotency-Key` and is answered from its binding.

post.summary:
Mint a track assistant conversation and deliver its first message, folded into one
`planner-harness-start` operation. Nothing on this path may read the
`harness.user_message.enqueued` row back: a failed attempt's row survives compensation
while the retry re-derives the same card id, so the row means "attempted", never "delivered".

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
**Required.** Scopes the derived card id and the operation dedup key, so retrying the same request can never mint a second conversation. A missing or blank header is 400.

**This is NOT standard HTTP idempotency — it is "same key = the same retryable draft"**: a success replays without re-sending; a terminal failure retries under a `#N` operation key; a stuck attempt stays failed closed; 64 failed attempts exhaust the key; and the same key with different text is a conflict. The derived card id never carries the retry suffix.

201.description: Conversation card minted, harness started, first message delivered — all three in the mint operation's own transaction, so a 201 means the message is on the assistant's queue and not merely that a card exists. Also returned when a retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` replays an earlier success (same conversation, no second message).

400.description: Missing/blank `Idempotency-Key`, or empty/over-long text. A `BadRequest` raised by `PlannerHarnessStartAdapter::validate` also lands here — the operation-failure mapping keeps `bad_request` a 400.

403.description: The track is retired hidden Area-chat scaffolding and cannot accept Track conversations.

409.description:
Distinguished by the body's `code`:
* `conflict` — the derived card already exists, or this `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a request whose first-message text differed (the text is bound into the operation payload, and its hash is what `submit` compares).
* `idempotency_key_exhausted` — the key used up its 64 retry slots; retry under a NEW `Idempotency-Key`.

500.description: Internal error. The message rides inside the mint operation, so the card and the delivery fail together: a terminally failed attempt is compensated (no card, no session) and the same `Idempotency-Key` retries under a `#N` operation key, re-deriving the same card id and delivering the message again. The `harness.user_message.enqueued` row a failed attempt already committed is NOT rolled back — `events` is append-only — and records only that a delivery was attempted, never that one happened. A previous attempt left `Stuck` also answers 500 under the same key until an operator clears it; there the card survives with the message still queued on a runtime that never started.

503.description: Shared codex app-server not running — retry shortly

AreaFolder.description:
One row per claimed directory; `path` is absolute and globally unique across the table. A folder
covers every descendant path, and overlapping claims are rejected.

AreaKind.description: Whether an area is user-visible or kernel-owned storage scaffolding.

default_cwd.description:
Missing leaves the preference alone, null restores managed workspaces,
and a string sets the exact attached working directory to preselect.

default_template_id.description:
Missing leaves the preference alone, null clears it, and a string sets
the built-in template preselected by the New Track surface.

AreaResolve.description: 200 body for `GET /api/areas/resolve`; the endpoint returns `null` (not 404) on miss.

AttachmentId.description:
`<uuid-v4>.<ext>` — an attachment's id *and* its file name. The only constructor is
[`AttachmentId::parse`] and `Deserialize` goes through the same gate.

childTrackId.description:
Written after claim, so exposing it preserves the read-state exception.
`spawn` must never be added beside it.

oneOf.description: Server-owned explanation for a task that has not started.

statusDetail.description: Failure classifier plus its human reason tail.

deletable.description:
System-card guard: `true` for user-facing cards, `false` for kernel-owned cards the user cannot
remove. Defaults to `true` because `bool::default()` is the unsafe fallback for a deny-by-omission auth bit.

kind.description:
`"terminal"` for built-in PTY cards, `"ui://<plugin>/<view>"` for plugin-provided cards.
`[legacy]` `"plugin:<plugin-id>:<view-id>"` may still appear on persisted rows.

deletable.description:
Not patchable via API: surfaced only so a client sending it gets a clear
400; `card_update_tx` never writes the column.

payload.description:
Replaces the stored payload. A payload carrying a server-owned key is refused with 400:
`terminal_signals`, `claude_permissions`, `claude_permissions_source`, `template_context`,
`planner_provider`. Every kernel-minted server-owned value the card already carries is kept.

CardRole.description: Authorization role persisted on each card and enforced by `role_gate`.

CardRuntimeView.description:
Live runtime projection read from `worker_sessions` when a card is fetched or serialized. Not
part of the idempotency contract: it may differ between a first POST response and a retry.

last_turn_completed_ms.description: When the card's last non-interrupted turn ended, or absent when it has none.

CatalogModel.description: One entry of the model catalog.

default_reasoning_effort.description:
The model's own default effort; `null` exactly when the provider offers no effort choice
(a Claude alias). Always a string for a Codex entry.

id.description:
Codex's preset identifier (a Claude alias for a Claude Planner), presentation only; never
send it back as a model selection.

is_default.description:
Codex's catalog-level default marker; not "what am I following now". Always `false` for
a Claude alias: the Claude CLI's default is the `null` selection.

model.description: The slug codex is invoked by, or the Claude alias passed as `--model`.

supported_reasoning_efforts.description: Empty for a Claude alias: a Claude Planner offers no effort choice.

ClaudePermissionsScope.description:
A declared Claude Code permission scope: the `claude_permissions` argument of `calm.terminal.open`
and the value of `tracks.claude_permissions_policy`. The derive is lenient on unknown keys on
purpose (stored rows from a newer binary); strictness lives in [`parse_scope_named`].

ConnectorInstall.description: The operator-supplied half of an `mcp-http` connector install.

api_key.description:
The credential. Absent or empty ⇒ an unauthenticated connector. Never echoed;
it reaches disk in `secrets.json` and nowhere else.

headers.description: Private literal HTTP headers. Stored only in secrets.json; not echoed.

tools_all.description: Explicit all-tools mode; omitted ⇒ the strict (possibly empty) allowlist.

CreateAreaRequest.description: User-facing Area creation. Deliberately permissive about unknown JSON keys: a caller-supplied `kind` must continue to be ignored rather than gaining a path to create a system Area.

sort.description: If absent, server appends to end.

CreateCardBody.description: Body payload accepted by `POST /api/tracks/:track_id/cards`: direct create (`kind`, `sort`, `payload`, `title`) or `via_tool_call`, which wins when both are sent.

kind.description: Legacy direct-create fields; `track_id` comes from the path.

oneOf.description: When present, the kernel calls the plugin and the `kind` / `payload` fields above are ignored.

Explicit authorization to create this track in `area_id` while its cwd remains covered
by the exact conflicting claim named here; checked inside the create transaction.

cwd.description:
Omitted / null persists `default_cwd()` and skips `area_folders`; present values
(including the empty string) keep the absolute-path + claim rules.

first_message.description:
The user's first sentence, seeded into the planner harness as a user message. Supplying
it makes `Idempotency-Key` required and turns a harness-start failure into a 500 (the
committed track is not undone).

fork_report_from.description:
One-time creation instruction: copy this track's report snapshot into the new report
inside the track-create transaction.

model.description:
Model slug for the planner's first and subsequent turns (a Claude alias for a `claude`
Planner). Omitted or null follows installation defaults, as on the conversation model
endpoint.

planner_provider.description:
The backend of the track's Planner, stamped on its card as the server-owned
`planner_provider` and never changed afterwards. `claude` is refused with 400 when the
server runs without `--claude-planner-config`, with a `model` that is not one of its
aliases, or with any `reasoning_effort`.

reasoning_effort.description:
Reasoning effort. Values unsupported by the chosen model's current
catalog entry are rejected with 400 before creation; no silent adjustment.
Omitted or null follows installation defaults. Must be omitted or null for `claude`.

recipe_id.description:
A user-defined recipe (`track_recipes` row) to start from. Not folded into
`template_id`: a recipe has no plugin manifest to resolve against.

template_id.description:
A built-in roster template to instantiate the report from; mutually exclusive with
`recipe_id` and `fork_report_from` (naming two is a 400).

title.description:
Omitted stores the empty string; the planner agent names the track via
`calm.track.rename` while the stored title is still blank.

if_entry_rev.description: The `rev` the client last read for this entry. Required.

message.description: Compatibility fields for existing MCP clients. `message` is always rendered from `code` + `message_args`.

if_entry_rev.description: The `rev` the client last read for this entry; a mismatch is a 409.

text.description: Replacement text, held to the same limits as `POST /planner/input`.

ErrorBody.description: JSON shape returned for every error response — `{error, code}`.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code (see `CalmError::code`). Three more are written by routes
directly: `forbidden_tool`, `not_a_card_tool`, `tool_call_failed`.

FolderConflict.description: 409 body for the folder-create conflict case.

FolderConflictKind.description: Kind of overlap detected by the `POST /api/areas/:area_id/folders` conflict check.

GetPlannerRunResponse.description: Current planner-harness run snapshot for a card, so a page opened mid-turn can seed its phase. Dormancy is NOT an error: it is the `{worker_session_id: null, phase: null}` answer.

attachments_supported.description: Whether this card can take image attachments at all: not when the track's workspace is an attached directory, since neige never writes into one. Answered by the same function the upload runs (`planner_attachments::attachment_root`).

blocked_reason.description:
Why this conversation's queue is not draining, or `null` when there is nothing worth saying: an undeterminable model/effort, a refused turn start, or a long codex outage. A client should render it as a standing notice, not a request error.
A brief outage fills nothing, so `null` is not evidence that anything succeeded.

model.description: The model slug this conversation's turns run with, or `null` to follow the installation default. Read off the CARD, so answered for a dormant conversation too.

pending.description: The addressable user entries still waiting for the next turn, in queue order. Empty when dormant. Dispatcher observations and pre-id user entries never appear; the latter are counted in `pending_overflow`.

pending_overflow.description: User-authored entries that exist in the queue but are NOT in `pending`: pre-id entries, plus anything past the page budget.

oneOf.description: Current harness phase, or null when the harness is dormant.

reasoning_effort.description: The chosen reasoning effort, or `null` for the default. Same source as `model`.

oneOf.description: Latest context-window usage, or null when the harness is dormant or codex has not pushed a `thread/tokenUsage/updated` frame yet. A dormant conversation reports `null` even though the reading is on disk.

worker_session_id.description: Active worker-session id, or null when the harness is dormant.

old_path.description: Previous path for renamed files, relative to the repository root.

path.description: Path relative to the repository root.

status.description: One of: modified, added, deleted, untracked, renamed.

path.description: Path relative to the repository root.

status.description: One of: modified, added, deleted, renamed.

HarnessInputPresentation.description:
How one segment of a harness `userMessage` should be presented to a human. The rendered English
is not a protocol: wording changes must not turn a system update into something the UI attributes to the user.

HarnessInputSegment.description: One observation in the exact order and wording sent to `turn/start`.

attachments.description: The images this segment carried into `turn/start`.

after_id.description: Return items with database ids greater than this value.

direction.description: Fetch the oldest (`asc`) or latest (`desc`) matching rows. Defaults to `asc`.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return. Defaults to 100 and is capped at 500.

allOf.description:
An `mcp-http` connector described by the request itself; the kernel synthesizes
the plugin tree and owns it thereafter.

oneOf.description:
An `mcp-http` connector described by the request itself; the kernel synthesizes
the plugin tree and owns it thereafter.

allOf.description:
A distinct source tag so older kernels reject the request instead of silently
ignoring `headers` and `tools_all`; `mcp_http` remains accepted.

oneOf.description:
A distinct source tag so older kernels reject the request instead of silently
ignoring `headers` and `tools_all`; `mcp_http` remains accepted.
Catch-all so tarball/url/etc. get a friendly 400 instead of a serde error.

stopped.description: True when a turn was running and an interrupt was dispatched at it; false when idle or a `turn/start` was still in flight. Means the interrupt was *issued* — completion is asynchronous.

entries.description:
Children, sorted: directories first, then case-insensitive alpha.
Conventional Unix dotfiles are included; `.` and `..` are excluded.

parent.description: Canonical absolute path of the parent directory, or `null` at root.

path.description: Canonical absolute path of the listed directory.

ModelDefaults.description: What a card that has selected nothing currently runs; `null` = not configured anywhere readable.

fetched_at_ms.description: Wall-clock ms at which the catalog was fetched, or `null` when it was not fetched.

sort.description: If absent, server appends to end.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path; the server trims a trailing slash (root `/` excepted).

track_id.description:
Defaulted so the REST handler can override from the `:track_id` path
param; direct repo callers must set it.

cwd.description:
Working directory Claude runs in. Empty string or missing -> `$HOME`
(then `cwd` of server).

icon_bg.description: Optional card-head logo background CSS color. Empty string is ignored.

icon_fg.description: Optional card-head logo foreground CSS color. Empty string is ignored.

prompt.description: Optional first prompt passed as Claude's positional prompt argument.

sort.description: Sort order within the track. `None` defaults to "append to end".

theme.description:
Host browser's current theme RGB. Required so the PTY daemon answers
Claude's terminal color probes with colors matching the surrounding UI.

NewCodexCardBody.description:
Body for `POST /api/tracks/:track_id/codex-cards`. Omits `kind` and `payload` (kernel-owned). A non-empty `prompt` starts a shared thread, sends it via `turn/start`, and starts the TUI as `codex resume`; empty means the user types.
`theme` is required with no default: a caller that forgets fails at compile time (TS) or with a 422.

cwd.description:
Working directory codex runs in. Empty string or missing → `$HOME`
(then `cwd` of server).

icon_bg.description: Optional card-head logo background CSS color. Empty string is ignored.

icon_fg.description: Optional card-head logo foreground CSS color. Empty string is ignored.

prompt.description: Hands-free seed prompt: when non-empty the kernel auto-submits it once codex's session is constructed.

sort.description: Sort order within the track. `None` defaults to "append to end".

theme.description: Host browser's current theme RGB, so the terminal model answers codex's OSC 10/11 startup probe with matching colors. Omitting it is a 422.

NewTerminalCardBody.description:
Body for `POST /api/tracks/:track_id/terminal-cards`. Omits `kind` (always
`"terminal"`) and `payload` (the kernel persists the schema payload).

cwd.description: Empty string or missing → the track's workspace path.

env.description: Extra env on top of the inherited set. JSON object: `{"FOO":"bar"}`.

sort.description: Sort order within the track. `None` defaults to "append to end".

theme.description:
Host browser's current theme RGB. Required — written onto the terminal row in the
same transaction that mints the card; every spawn reads it for `--terminal-fg/-bg`.

attach_folder.description:
Claim `cwd` for `area_id` as a new folder in the same transaction as the
track create. Default `false`: the cwd must already be covered by a folder.

cwd.description:
Absolute path the planner daemon spawns under; the route validates,
`track_create_tx` writes verbatim.

plugin_scope.description: Copied from the owning Manifest at create; not accepted on `POST /api/tracks`.

template_input.description:
JSON input for the bound template: validated against the Manifest's
`input_schema` by the route, persisted verbatim, never interpreted by the kernel.

theme.description:
Host browser's theme RGB, required so the planner card's terminal answers
codex's OSC 10/11 probe with matching colors. Tests use `default_dark()`.

model.description: Explicit choice for the first turn; omitted/null follows the installation default.

text.description:
The first message. Validated exactly like `POST /api/cards/{id}/planner/input`, and
before anything is minted, so a rejected message leaves no card behind.

kind.description: Plugin-defined string. Kernel does not interpret.

entity_id.description: Optional. When omitted, returns every overlay of `entity_kind` across the workspace.

PendingQueueEntry.description: One addressable user entry from the harness pending queue.

attachments.description: The images this queued message carries. Each is already bound; the client addresses an attachment by id, never by host path.

entry_id.description: Stable identity. Never empty, and unique within one response: the snapshot decoder refuses an empty or duplicated id, demoting the slot to `LegacyUser`.

queued_at_ms.description: Wall-clock ms at which the entry entered the queue.

rev.description: CAS token for the edit/delete endpoints. Bumped whenever the text is rewritten, folding included.

text.description: The complete text. Never truncated — an entry that would not fit the page budget is left out entirely.

PlannerAttachment.description: One attachment as the frontend sees it in a queue entry or a transcript segment.

url.description: Where to read the bytes; derived by [`attachment_url`]. The server's host path is NOT here and must not be.

rev.description:
The entry's `rev` after the change. On a delete this is the rev it
carried when it left, so a client can tell which read it acted on.

text.description: The entry's text after an edit; null for a delete.

PlannerInputStaleBody.description: 409 body for a compare-and-swap failure; carries the current text and rev.

rev.description: The entry's current rev — resend with this to overwrite deliberately.

text.description: The entry's text as it stands now.

PlannerRunTokenUsage.description: The context-usage half of [`GetPlannerRunResponse`]. `percent` is computed on the server so there is one place to get it wrong, and `total_tokens` is NOT shipped: it is a cumulative sum across the thread, and a meter drawn from it is the most likely UI bug.

at_ms.description: Wall-clock ms of the codex frame this reading came from. The reading survives a reboot via the runtime snapshot, so without this a rehydrated reading is indistinguishable from a live one.

context_window.description: The model's context window, or null when codex has never reported one.

percent.description: Context occupancy as a whole percentage, `0.0..=100.0`. Null when no percentage can honestly be stated (no window, window at or below baseline, or usage above the window — deliberately NOT clamped).

used_tokens.description: Tokens in the model's context as of the most recent response. Always present, even when `percent` is not.

PlannerSteerConflictBody.description:
The steer route's 409: two typed shapes told apart by `code`. utoipa binds one
body per status, so the pair is declared as this untagged union.

PlannerSteerRefusedBody.description:
409 body for a steer that delivered nothing (`planner_steer_no_running_turn`: the
message is still queued with the `rev` the client read) or nothing known
(`planner_steer_unknown_outcome`: codex did not answer, so the message is queued
again but may also have reached the turn).

PlannerSteerResponse.description: What a steer answers on success: codex has the message inside `turn_id`.

steered.description: Always `true` on a 200; refusals are typed 409s, never `false` here.

turn_id.description: The turn that took the message — the one that was running.

PluginDetail.description: Single-plugin detail; the full manifest blob rides along.

config_schema.description:
The schema the config form renders from, read from the registry — authoritative
over `manifest.config_schema`, which is the persisted blob and may be stale.
`None` means no schema is in force.

effective_config.description:
`defaults ⊕ user_config`, i.e. what the plugin runs with. Carried alongside
`user_config` so a form can tell an operator's choice from a manifest default and
never posts defaults back to be persisted.

user_config.description:
What the operator has actually **set** — the persisted row, verbatim,
with no defaults folded in.

PluginListItem.description: Compact row used by `GET /api/plugins`; the full manifest is excluded to keep the list cheap.

has_config.description:
Does this plugin declare a `config_schema`? Read from the registry, the same source
the write path validates against; `false` when the manifest is not loaded.

state.description:
Wire-name string: `running | spawning | crashed | unavailable | disabled | installing
| installed`. `unavailable` is a normal terminal state: no process was started,
nothing is watching, and nothing will retry until an operator intervenes.

ReasoningEffortOption.description: One selectable reasoning effort for a model.

reasoning_effort.description:
A bare string, never a closed enum: codex's `ReasoningEffort` carries a
`Custom(String)` variant and accepts any non-empty string on the wire.

ReportBlock.description: A derived, addressable slice of a track report.

ReportSeriesDetail.description:
`?detail=`: `full` (the default) attaches every series' `points`; `summary` answers
with the stored summary only.

ReportSeriesEntry.description:
One series inside `ReportSeriesResolved.series` — the stored summary
(`summary::SeriesSummary`, verbatim) plus `points` on a `full` read.

change_pct.description:
`(last - first) / first * 100`, two decimals; `null` when `first`
is zero.

complete_through.description:
The latest daily bar the source had published when the row was
resolved (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

points.description:
`full` only: `[[ts_ms, value], …]`, or `[[ts_ms, open, high, low,
close, volume], …]` for `view: candles`. `ts_ms` is UTC midnight.

status.description:
`ok`, or the plugin's verdict for this asset (`unknown_asset`,
`unavailable`), in which case only `reason` accompanies it.

ReportSeriesResolved.description:
The flattened `resolved` object — the same shape `calm.report.read`
attaches to a `chart.series` block, with the block's presentation
fields (`view` / `field` / `period` / `range`) alongside.

as_of.description:
`ok`: the cutoff the data runs through (`YYYY-MM-DD`) — the payload's
`as_of` for a frozen block, yesterday UTC at resolution for a live one.

pinned.description:
`ok`: a frozen block whose source has published past `as_of`; the row
is immutable from then on.

reason.description:
`unavailable`: why. `pending`: present when the read could not even
queue a job (plugin not installed / not running / tool not exposed).

resolved_at.description: `ok` / `unavailable`: when the row was written, RFC 3339 UTC.

series.description:
`ok`: one entry per requested asset, in request order. Absent on the
other two statuses.

status.description:
`pending` (no row yet — the read just queued one), `unavailable`
(the last resolution failed; see `reason`) or `ok`.

ReportSeriesRevConflict.description: The 409 body: the block moved on since the caller read the report.

RequestTheme.description:
Wire shape of `NewCodexCardBody.theme` / `NewTrack.theme`; duplicates
`calm_session::TerminalTheme` so the route keeps its own `ToSchema`.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to resolve against every area's folder claims; `null` if no claim covers it.

attachments.description:
Ids returned by `POST /api/cards/{id}/planner/attachments`. Naming an attachment here is what BINDS it: the bytes move out of the sweepable staging area before this request writes anything to the queue.
An id belonging to another card is a 400, as is naming the same one twice or naming more than eight.

entry_id.description: Stable id of the queue entry this text landed in, so the client can match its optimistic echo. Null only when the text folded into a pre-id queue entry.

model.description:
The model **slug** to run with (never a catalog entry's `id`; a Claude alias for a Claude
Planner), or `null` to follow the installation default (for a Claude Planner, the Claude
CLI's own). `#[schema(required = true)]` is needed because utoipa
derives optionality from the `Option<T>` alone and cannot see `deserialize_with`.

reasoning_effort.description:
The reasoning effort, or `null` to follow the default. Required. A bare string:
codex accepts any non-empty effort. Always `null` for a Claude Planner.

effort_adjusted.description:
The requested effort was not supported by the chosen model and was moved to that
model's own default.

model.description: The stored slug, echoed rather than assumed.

reasoning_effort.description: The stored effort. Differs from the request when `effort_adjusted`.

unknown_model.description:
The slug is not in the catalog codex currently reports. A hint, not a refusal;
always `false` when the catalog could not be read.

SettingsBag.description: Wire-shape: a flat string map of key -> value; `BTreeMap` for deterministic ordering.

SettingsPutBody.description: Request body for `PUT /api/settings`. `null` and `""` both clear a key.

oneOf.description: The recorded plugin call the body was read off.

args_canon.description: Canonicalization version behind `args_sha256` (`v1`: compact serde_json text with sorted keys).

SourceOrigin.description: Where a body came from. Stored verbatim as the row's `origin` column.

SourceProvenance.description:
What the body *is*: the Planner's declaration, page-visible. `manual` bodies are the Planner's
own and are marked as not kernel-verified.

SourceQuote.description: One anchor of a source: `text` is a byte-exact substring of the body (`body[start..end]`, UTF-8 byte offsets).

SteerPlannerInputBody.description: Body of `POST …/{entry_id}/steer`: the same compare-and-swap token as the delete.

TaskAttemptView.description:
Execution summary. Status includes awaiting_projection when admission capacity removed a pending row.
Blocking reason applies only to the selected current attempt; historical attempts carry null.

TaskRecoveryReceipt.description: Stable acknowledgement, including when the response to the first call was lost.

TaskRecoveryView.description:
Execution history. `current` is null only when the live declaration has never
received an allocation.

exit_code.description:
Exit code captured at `child.wait()`; `None` = not exited, signal-killed,
or daemon lost. `required = true` makes the OpenAPI field
required-but-nullable so clients get `number | null`, not `?:`.

pid.description: Child process id; `None` for rows whose spawn returned no pid.

pty_output.description: Bounded tail of the merged PTY byte stream, decoded lossily as UTF-8.

pty_output_truncated.description:
True when bytes were dropped before `pty_output`, either by the
supervisor replay window or the smaller durable-evidence cap.

signal_killed.description:
True when the child was killed by a signal; mutually exclusive with
`exit_code.is_some()` at the writer.

theme_bg.description: Host browser's background RGB at row-creation; written together with `theme_fg`.

theme_fg.description: Host browser's foreground RGB at row-creation, comma-decimal `r,g,b`.

report_has_noninitial_content.description: Always `false` on success; returned rather than assumed so a caller sees the reset land.

track_id.description: The launchpad track whose report was restored.

TodayLaunchpadResolved.description: What the Today page load reads: a narrow, read-only DTO, distinct from [`TodayLaunchpad`].

report_has_noninitial_content.description:
Whether this report holds content right now beyond the empty skeleton — a statement
about CURRENT content, not history: restoring the canonical text flips it back to
`false`, and a user hand-edit flips it exactly as a summary agent would. The frontend
must not re-derive this from the report body.

TodaySummaryStarted.description: What the caller gets back on success.

card_id.description: The summary conversation's card. Stable for the launchpad's lifetime.

track_id.description: The launchpad track, whose report the agent is being asked to rewrite.

ToolCallBody.description:
AppBridge → kernel tool-call wire body, mirroring the JSON-RPC `tools/call` params
shape. `call_id` is threaded into every event written while servicing the call as
`correlation = "user_tool_call:<call_id>"`.

call_id.description: Optional caller-supplied tracing id; absent ⇒ `correlation = NULL`.

oneOf.description:
The user-set Claude Code permission policy of this track's TREE, stored on the tree root only;
a child row is always `null` here even when its root carries a policy.

cwd.description: Wire-compatibility alias of `workspace.path`, serialized as `cwd`; Rust readers must use `workspace.path`.

plugin_scope.description: The plugin that owns this track, recorded when the row is created.

purpose.description: Server-owned structural marker. Public track creation cannot set this.

recipe_id.description: The user recipe ([`TrackRecipe`]) this track was instantiated from; may name a recipe that no longer exists.

recipe_revision.description: The recipe's `revision` at the moment this track was created.

template_id.description: Template this track was created from. Names the birth snapshot only.

template_input.description: Template input is validated at creation and otherwise remains opaque.

terminal_at.description: Unix-ms timestamp the track most recently entered a terminal lifecycle state, or `None` while non-terminal.

TrackBacklink.description: A report link from another track that targets this track.

TrackBacklinksResponse.description: A bounded page of report backlinks.

id.description: The assistant card's id; the conversation's identity everywhere.

kind.description: Always `"track-assistant"`, derived from the card's persisted marker.

lastTurnCompletedAt.description: When the conversation's last non-interrupted turn ended, or `null` when there is none.

oneOf.description: The live session's state, or **null when the card has no session row**. Never fill it with an invented value.

title.description: The conversation's own name, or null before it has one.

trackId.description: The track this conversation lives on.

updatedAt.description: The session's last update, falling back to the card's own.

can_resume.description:
Lifecycle permission and child-track integrity resolved together so
clients never advertise an action the write must reject.

path.description: Logical path to list. Omitted or `/` lists the track root.

TrackLifecycle.description:
Track lifecycle state machine. `archived` is intentionally NOT a lifecycle state: archival lives
on `archived_at`, orthogonal to execution semantics.

TrackPatch.description: `plugin_scope` is create-time only and is not a field here. Extra JSON keys are ignored.

archived_at.description:
Pass `Some(Some(ts))` to archive, `Some(None)` to unarchive,
or omit (`None`) to leave alone.

automation_policy.description: Per-track declaration policy. A present null resets to the kernel default.

oneOf.description:
Claude Code permission policy of the WHOLE track tree; tree-root-only.
`Some(None)` clears. Read through `parse_scope_named`, so a bad shape is an
error naming the field, never a lenient decode.

Request a lifecycle transition; validated through `crate::track_lifecycle`
inside the write transaction.

pinned_at.description:
Pass `Some(Some(ts))` to pin, `Some(None)` to unpin,
or omit (`None`) to leave alone.

planner_task_ceiling.description:
Maximum admitted planner-declared task inventory. A present null resets to
the kernel default.

require_task_gates.description: Track-level gate policy; `Some(v)` sets the flag.

task_budget.description: Per-track scheduler budget; `Some(None)` clears back to the kernel default.

tree_task_budget.description:
Budget for the non-terminal planner inventory of the WHOLE track tree.
Root-only; a present null resets to the kernel default (32).

oneOf.description:
Request a workspace change. Handled by the route, never by
`track_update_tx`: a re-point is a filesystem move bracketed by two
transactions, and mutually exclusive with every other field here.

live.description: Whether the dev server behind it accepted a TCP connection just now.

port.description: The gateway pool port the browser loads.

TrackRecipe.description:
A user-defined starting point for a new track: a saved report whose `title` doubles as the
summary and whose `neige-block` fences are its tasks.

body.description: Report body. Its `neige-block` fences are the tasks.

revision.description: Optimistic-lock anchor. Writers pass the revision they read and the UPDATE validates + bumps in one statement.

title.description: Picker label *and* the instantiated report's summary.

updated_at.description: Display only — never a lock anchor. See `revision`.

TrackReportPayload.description:
The payload persisted in a track-report card's `payload` JSON column; `summary` is the one-line
preview, `body` the Markdown source the TrackReportCard renders.

blocks.description:
Block mirror of the authoritative CRDT block map; this field and `body` are both projections the
persist boundary rewrites on every write. v1 rows may omit it.

body.description: Markdown source. Sections are derived at render time by splitting at H1 (`^# `) headings.

docRev.description: Document-wide optimistic-concurrency revision, mirrored from the authoritative CRDT root.

schemaVersion.description: Tier A persistence contract; older rows remain readable and are lazily upgraded at the next persist.

summary.description: One-line summary used by sidebars / track-list previews; empty string is valid.

TrackSourceDetail.description: A captured source with its body: the raw text the kernel stored, verbatim.

TrackSourceSummary.description: A captured source without its body.

TrackTemplate.description:
One selectable starting point for a new track. "Blank" is not in this list: it is
the absence of a template, rendered by the client as its own default option.

id.description: Template key. Passed back verbatim as `template_id` on `POST /api/tracks`.

input_schema.description:
JSON Schema for `template_input`, from the manifest of the running trusted plugin
bound to `id`. Absent means the template takes no input.

tasks.description: The tasks this template pre-sets, in plan order. Always present; not always non-empty.

TrackTemplateTask.description: One pre-set task, projected from a `task` fence in the template file's body.

goal.description: What that task is for, verbatim from the template.

key.description: The task block's `key` in the recipe this template instantiates to.

TrackWorkspace.description: A track's typed workspace. `path` is its single stored path.

frozen_at.description:
One-shot, monotonic. `Some` ⇒ neither `path` nor `kind` may change again. The system-area
launchpad stays unfrozen because it is repointed.

TrackWorkspaceKind.description: Ownership must be explicit because only managed workspaces may be recycled.

TrackWorkspacePatch.description:
Point a track at a repository the user already has. The only transition is
`managed → attached`: a managed path is derived from area and id, and
`attached → *` stays refused, so this is a one-way door stamping `frozen_at`.

attach_folder.description:
Claim `path` for this track's area in the same transaction. Default
`false`: an unclaimed path is refused rather than making a homeless track.

kind.description: Must be `attached`. `managed` is a documented 400, not a silent no-op.

path.description: Absolute path to an existing Git work tree, validated before anything is written.

TracksWindowQuery.description:
Calendar window query parameters for `GET /api/tracks`; `since` / `until` are
inclusive at both endpoints.

area_id.description:
Optional per-area filter. Mirrors `list_tracks_by_area` for
callers that want one area's window in a single endpoint.

since.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) in unix milliseconds. Track is included
when `terminal_at IS NULL OR terminal_at >= since`. Omitting
disables the lower-bound filter.

until.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) in unix milliseconds. Track is included
when `created_at <= until`. Omitting disables the upper-bound
filter.

if_revision.description: The `revision` the caller read. A mismatch is 409 — never a silent overwrite.

body.description:
Markdown source. Sections are derived at render time by
splitting at H1 (`^# `) headings; the kernel does not interpret
the structure.

ifDocRev.description:
Expected document revision from the latest report read. Use zero
for a document that has never been persisted through the CRDT path.

summary.description:
One-line summary the track-list sidebars surface. Empty string
is a valid value; the caller must commit.

url.description:
Absolute REST path the browser reads the bytes back from. Durable only once the attachment is
bound: a staged upload never sent is swept after the 24h orphan TTL, after which this path answers 400.

VersionInfo.description: Response shape for `GET /api/version`; camelCase on the wire.

apiVersion.description:
REST contract version. Diagnostic-only on the wire — the frontend gates on
`min_web_compat_version` and `sync_event_version`.

areaCreateIdempotency.description: True only when Area creation binds Idempotency-Key atomically and permanently.

conversationCreateModel.description: First-message model selection is part of atomic conversation creation.

databaseId.description:
The database's stable id, minted once into the one-row `database_identity` table;
survives restarts where `db_instance_id` does not.

dbInstanceId.description: UUID v4 minted once per process boot.

nowMs.description: The server clock (unix ms) when this response was built.
